HASTS206 Assignment 2 – Applied Demographic Analysis¶

University of Zimbabwe · Department of Mathematics and Computational Sciences · Lecturer: Mr. G. Mazivisa

All figures in this notebook come from the synthetic (hypothetical) teaching dataset supplied with the assignment. They do not describe real Zimbabwean districts or insured lives.

The analysis is split into ten parts. Each part below shows the code of the matching file in src/ and then its output (tables, checks and plots). The same code runs from the command line with python src/run_all.py.

Part 1 – Load and inspect the supplied files¶

Written by Lennox Tawanda Jaricha (Project Lead and Data Engineer) · file src/part01_load_and_inspect_Lennox_Tawanda_Jaricha.py We read the five CSVs from data/raw/ without changing them and compare the row counts with the dataset README.

In [2]:
# ---- Code from src/part01_load_and_inspect_Lennox_Tawanda_Jaricha.py ----
"""
Author: Lennox Tawanda Jaricha    |    Role: Project Lead and Data Engineer    |    Checked by: Trish Tembo
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 1 - Load the supplied CSVs and take a first look.

We keep the original files untouched in data/raw/ and only work on copies in
memory. Cleaning decisions are recorded in Part 2 (data-quality log).
"""
import pandas as pd

from common import load_raw, show_table, save_table, HYPO


def main():
    print("Author: Lennox Tawanda Jaricha (Project Lead and Data Engineer)")
    print(f"PART 1: Loading data ({HYPO})")
    data = load_raw()

    # Shape and dtypes of every file
    rows = []
    for name, df in data.items():
        rows.append({
            "file": name,
            "rows": len(df),
            "columns": df.shape[1],
            "missing_cells": int(df.isna().sum().sum()),
            "column_names": ", ".join(df.columns),
        })
    overview = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    show_table(overview, "File overview")
    save_table(overview, "p01_file_overview.csv")

    # Peek at each file
    for name, df in data.items():
        show_table(df.head(4), f"First rows of {name}")

    # Expected sizes from the dataset README
    expected = {"districts": 24, "age_sex": 864, "life": 18, "scen": 3, "ins": 96}
    for name, n in expected.items():
        status = "OK" if len(data[name]) == n else "MISMATCH"
        print(f"  {name:<10} rows = {len(data[name]):>4}  expected {n:>4}  -> {status}")
    return data


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Part 2 – Data-quality log¶

Written by Emeldah Munyanyi (Data Quality Analyst) · file src/part02_data_quality_Emeldah_Munyanyi.py Every check is written to outputs/tables/p02_data_quality_log.csv. Two points matter for the rest of the work:

  • Missing water values for D04 and D17 are kept blank in the clean file and only imputed for clustering (Part 9).
  • Scope of deaths. District deaths_2025 include deaths among babies born during 2025, while baseline_deaths_2025 in the age–sex file only covers people already alive on 1 January 2025 (classified by age at baseline). So the district figure is always larger; the gap (7 to 47 per district, 621 overall) is the deaths among 2025 births.
In [3]:
# ---- Code from src/part02_data_quality_Emeldah_Munyanyi.py ----
"""
Author: Emeldah Munyanyi    |    Role: Data Quality Analyst    |    Checked by: Gogodi Vimbai
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 2 - Data-quality log and cleaning decisions.

The brief asks us to check row counts, keys, join cardinality, age-band and sex
coverage, missing indicators and valid ranges, and to reconcile population
totals and event counts where the definitions allow. Every check is written to
outputs/tables/p02_data_quality_log.csv so the log is reproducible.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import load_raw, show_table, save_table

LOG = []


def log(file, check, result, status, action="None needed"):
    LOG.append({"check_no": len(LOG) + 1, "file": file, "check": check,
                "result": result, "status": status, "decision_or_action": action})


def main():
    print("Author: Emeldah Munyanyi (Data Quality Analyst)")
    print("PART 2: Data-quality log, reconciliations and cleaning decisions")
    LOG.clear()
    d = load_raw()
    dist, ags, life, scen, ins = d["districts"], d["age_sex"], d["life"], d["scen"], d["ins"]

    # ---------------- 1. Row counts --------------------------------------
    for name, df, n in [("districts.csv", dist, 24), ("age_sex.csv", ags, 864),
                        ("life_table_inputs.csv", life, 18),
                        ("projection_scenarios.csv", scen, 3),
                        ("insured_transitions.csv", ins, 96)]:
        log(name, "Row count vs README", f"{len(df)} rows (expected {n})",
            "PASS" if len(df) == n else "FAIL")

    # ---------------- 2. Primary keys ------------------------------------
    keys = [("districts.csv", dist, ["district_id"]),
            ("age_sex.csv", ags, ["district_id", "age_start", "sex"]),
            ("life_table_inputs.csv", life, ["age_start"]),
            ("projection_scenarios.csv", scen, ["scenario"]),
            ("insured_transitions.csv", ins, ["district_id", "origin", "destination"])]
    for name, df, k in keys:
        dups = int(df.duplicated(k).sum())
        log(name, f"Key {'+'.join(k)} unique", f"{dups} duplicate keys",
            "PASS" if dups == 0 else "FAIL")

    # ---------------- 3. Join cardinality --------------------------------
    per_dist = ags.groupby("district_id").size()
    log("age_sex.csv -> districts.csv", "Join cardinality (many-to-one)",
        f"{per_dist.nunique()} distinct row count(s) per district: {[int(v) for v in sorted(per_dist.unique())]}; "
        f"{ags.district_id.nunique()} districts matched",
        "PASS" if set(ags.district_id) == set(dist.district_id) and per_dist.eq(36).all() else "FAIL")
    m = ags.merge(dist[["district_id"]], on="district_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
    log("age_sex.csv -> districts.csv", "Unmatched rows after left join",
        f"{(m['_merge'] != 'both').sum()} unmatched", "PASS")
    per_ins = ins.groupby("district_id").size()
    log("insured_transitions.csv -> districts.csv", "Join cardinality (many-to-one)",
        f"4 rows per district for all {per_ins.size} districts" if per_ins.eq(4).all() else "Irregular",
        "PASS" if per_ins.eq(4).all() and set(ins.district_id) == set(dist.district_id) else "FAIL")

    # ---------------- 4. Age-band and sex coverage -----------------------
    bands = sorted(ags.age_start.unique())
    log("age_sex.csv", "Age bands present", f"{len(bands)} bands: {bands[0]} to {bands[-1]} in steps of 5",
        "PASS" if bands == list(range(0, 90, 5)) else "FAIL")
    log("age_sex.csv", "Sex codes", f"values = {sorted(ags.sex.unique())}",
        "PASS" if set(ags.sex) == {"F", "M"} else "FAIL")
    full = ags.groupby(["district_id"]).apply(lambda g: len(set(zip(g.age_start, g.sex))), include_groups=False)
    log("age_sex.csv", "Every district has all 18 bands x 2 sexes", f"min combos = {full.min()}",
        "PASS" if full.min() == 36 else "FAIL")
    log("life_table_inputs.csv", "Life-table age bands", f"{life.age_start.min()} to {life.age_start.max()}, {len(life)} bands",
        "PASS" if list(life.age_start) == list(range(0, 90, 5)) else "FAIL")

    # ---------------- 5. Missing indicators ------------------------------
    miss = dist.piped_water_pct.isna()
    log("districts.csv", "Missing piped_water_pct", f"{miss.sum()} missing: {', '.join(dist.district_id[miss])}",
        "FLAG", "Kept blank in the clean file; imputed only for clustering (Part 9, KNN rule)")
    for name, df in [("age_sex.csv", ags), ("projection_scenarios.csv", scen), ("insured_transitions.csv", ins)]:
        log(name, "Missing values", f"{int(df.isna().sum().sum())} missing cells",
            "PASS" if df.isna().sum().sum() == 0 else "FLAG")
    open_row = life[life.age_start == 85]
    log("life_table_inputs.csv", "Blank interval_years and ax at 85+",
        f"interval blank={open_row.interval_years.isna().all()}, ax blank={open_row.ax.isna().all()}",
        "NOTE", "Structural: open interval. We use q85+=1 and L85+=l85/m85+")

    # ---------------- 6. Valid ranges -----------------------------------
    count_cols = ["population_2025", "baseline_deaths_2025", "arrivals_2025", "departures_2025", "births_to_women_2025"]
    neg = int((ags[count_cols] < 0).sum().sum())
    nonint = int((ags[count_cols] % 1 != 0).sum().sum())
    log("age_sex.csv", "Counts non-negative integers", f"{neg} negative, {nonint} non-integer", "PASS" if neg + nonint == 0 else "FAIL")
    s = ags.survival_5yr
    log("age_sex.csv", "survival_5yr in (0,1]", f"min={s.min():.4f}, max={s.max():.4f}", "PASS" if s.gt(0).all() and s.le(1).all() else "FAIL")
    male_births = int(ags.loc[ags.sex == "M", "births_to_women_2025"].sum())
    log("age_sex.csv", "Births on male rows", f"total = {male_births}", "PASS" if male_births == 0 else "FAIL",
        "Structural zeros kept; births summed over female rows only")
    fert_ages = sorted(ags.loc[(ags.sex == "F") & (ags.births_to_women_2025 > 0), "age_start"].unique())
    log("age_sex.csv", "Ages with births (mother's baseline age)", f"{fert_ages[0]} to {fert_ages[-1] + 4}",
        "PASS" if fert_ages[0] >= 10 and fert_ages[-1] <= 45 else "FLAG")
    over = int((ags.baseline_deaths_2025 > ags.population_2025).sum())
    log("age_sex.csv", "Deaths <= baseline population", f"{over} rows violate", "PASS" if over == 0 else "FAIL")
    w = dist.piped_water_pct.dropna()
    log("districts.csv", "piped_water_pct within 0-100", f"min={w.min()}, max={w.max()}", "PASS" if w.between(0, 100).all() else "FAIL")
    ev = dist[["population_2020", "population_2026", "births_2025", "deaths_2025", "arrivals_2025", "departures_2025"]]
    log("districts.csv", "Population and events non-negative", f"{int((ev < 0).sum().sum())} negatives", "PASS")
    log("life_table_inputs.csv", "deaths < person_years and ax < interval",
        f"max m = {(life.deaths / life.person_years).max():.4f}; ax/n max = {(life.ax / life.interval_years).max():.2f}",
        "PASS" if (life.deaths < life.person_years).all() and (life.ax.dropna() < life.interval_years.dropna()).all() else "FAIL")
    ok_scen = scen[["fertility_multiplier", "arrivals_multiplier", "departures_multiplier"]].gt(0).all().all() and \
        scen[["newborn_survival_f", "newborn_survival_m"]].apply(lambda c: c.between(0, 1)).all().all()
    log("projection_scenarios.csv", "Multipliers > 0, newborn survival in [0,1]",
        "Low/Base/High present" if set(scen.scenario) == {"Low", "Base", "High"} else "Scenario missing",
        "PASS" if ok_scen else "FAIL")

    # Insured repeated-field rules
    rep_exp = ins.groupby(["district_id", "origin"]).exposure_py.nunique().max()
    rep_lives = ins.groupby(["district_id", "origin"]).initial_lives.nunique().max()
    log("insured_transitions.csv", "Exposure and initial_lives repeated identically across destinations",
        f"max distinct exposure per district-origin = {rep_exp}; initial_lives = {rep_lives}",
        "PASS" if rep_exp == 1 and rep_lives == 1 else "FAIL",
        "Counted once per district-origin (README rule) to avoid double counting")
    pairs = set(zip(ins.origin, ins.destination))
    log("insured_transitions.csv", "Allowed transitions", f"{sorted(pairs)}",
        "PASS" if pairs == {("H", "I"), ("H", "D"), ("I", "H"), ("I", "D")} else "FAIL")
    log("insured_transitions.csv", "Counts non-negative and exposure > 0",
        f"min count={ins.transition_count.min()}, min exposure={ins.exposure_py.min()}", "PASS")

    # ---------------- 7. Reconciliations ---------------------------------
    g = ags.groupby("district_id")
    rec = dist.set_index("district_id")[["population_2026", "births_2025", "deaths_2025", "arrivals_2025", "departures_2025"]].copy()
    rec["population_2025_agesex"] = g.population_2025.sum()
    rec["births_female_rows"] = g.births_to_women_2025.sum()
    rec["arrivals_agesex"] = g.arrivals_2025.sum()
    rec["departures_agesex"] = g.departures_2025.sum()
    rec["baseline_deaths_agesex"] = g.baseline_deaths_2025.sum()
    rec["deaths_among_2025_births"] = rec.deaths_2025 - rec.baseline_deaths_agesex
    rec["balance_2026"] = (rec.population_2025_agesex + rec.births_2025 - rec.deaths_2025
                           + rec.arrivals_2025 - rec.departures_2025)
    rec["balance_gap"] = rec.population_2026 - rec.balance_2026
    save_table(rec.reset_index(), "p02_reconciliation_by_district.csv")

    log("age_sex vs districts", "Births: female rows vs district births_2025",
        f"max abs gap = {int((rec.births_female_rows - rec.births_2025).abs().max())}",
        "PASS" if (rec.births_female_rows == rec.births_2025).all() else "FLAG")
    log("age_sex vs districts", "Arrivals and departures by age-sex vs district totals",
        f"max gaps = {int((rec.arrivals_agesex - rec.arrivals_2025).abs().max())}, "
        f"{int((rec.departures_agesex - rec.departures_2025).abs().max())}",
        "PASS" if (rec.arrivals_agesex == rec.arrivals_2025).all() and (rec.departures_agesex == rec.departures_2025).all() else "FLAG")
    log("age_sex vs districts", "Deaths: district deaths minus baseline deaths (scope difference)",
        f"gap between {int(rec.deaths_among_2025_births.min())} and {int(rec.deaths_among_2025_births.max())} "
        f"per district, total {int(rec.deaths_among_2025_births.sum())}; all positive = {(rec.deaths_among_2025_births > 0).all()}",
        "NOTE", "Not an error: district deaths also include deaths among babies born in 2025; "
                "the age-sex file only covers residents present on 1 Jan 2025")
    log("districts.csv", "Balancing equation closes at 1 Jan 2026",
        f"max abs gap = {int(rec.balance_gap.abs().max())} persons over 24 districts",
        "PASS" if rec.balance_gap.abs().max() == 0 else "FLAG")
    log("all files", "Original CSVs retained", "data/raw/ is read-only input; clean copy written to outputs/tables", "NOTE")

    # ---------------- 8. Cleaning decisions -> clean copies ---------------
    clean_dist = dist.copy()
    clean_dist["population_2025"] = clean_dist.district_id.map(rec.population_2025_agesex)
    clean_dist["water_missing_flag"] = clean_dist.piped_water_pct.isna().astype(int)
    save_table(clean_dist, "clean_districts.csv")
    clean_ags = ags.copy()
    clean_ags["age_group"] = clean_ags.age_start.map(lambda a: "85+" if a == 85 else f"{a}-{a + 4}")
    save_table(clean_ags, "clean_age_sex.csv")
    log("clean files", "Cleaning decisions applied",
        "Added population_2025 (sum of age-sex) and missing-water flag to districts; added age_group labels",
        "NOTE", "No rows dropped, no values changed")

    qlog = pd.DataFrame(LOG)
    save_table(qlog, "p02_data_quality_log.csv")
    show_table(qlog[["check_no", "file", "check", "result", "status"]], "Data-quality log")
    print("\nStatus summary:", qlog.status.value_counts().to_dict())
    show_table(rec[["population_2025_agesex", "births_2025", "births_female_rows", "deaths_2025",
                    "baseline_deaths_agesex", "deaths_among_2025_births", "balance_gap"]].head(8),
               "Reconciliation (first 8 districts)")
    return qlog, rec


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Part 3 – District selection, pyramids and ratios (Q1a)¶

Written by Mlungisi Ncube K (Population Structure Analyst) · file src/part03_selection_pyramids_ratios_Mlungisi_Ncube_K.py We chose D13 and D24: they are almost the same size (about 173,000 people), so a common scale compares shape rather than size, and they sit at opposite ends of the age-structure range. D13 is also used for the projection.

In [4]:
# ---- Code from src/part03_selection_pyramids_ratios_Mlungisi_Ncube_K.py ----
"""
Author: Mlungisi Ncube K    |    Role: Population Structure Analyst    |    Checked by: Ketso Thabiso Mdlongwa
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 3 - District selection, population pyramids and dependency ratios (Q1a).

Selection rule we agreed as a group:
  * Look at all 24 districts on the share under 15, share 65+, crude birth and
    death rates and the net migration rate.
  * Pick two districts of almost the same total size (so the pyramids on a
    common scale compare shape, not size) that sit at opposite ends of the
    age-structure range.
  * D13 is the largest of the young, high-fertility, net out-migration
    districts; D24 is the largest of the old, natural-decrease districts.
    Both have about 173,000 residents on 1 January 2025.
  * D13 is used for the age-sex projection because its fertility assumptions
    matter most for planning (schools, maternal and child health).
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import (load_raw, show_table, save_table, save_fig, save_settings, plt,
                    DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE, HYPO, age_label)


def district_screen(dist, ags):
    """One row per district with the indicators used to choose the pair."""
    p25 = ags.groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum()
    u15 = ags[ags.age_start < 15].groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum()
    o65 = ags[ags.age_start >= 65].groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum()
    t = dist.set_index("district_id").copy()
    t["population_2025"] = p25
    t["exposure_2025"] = (t.population_2025 + t.population_2026) / 2
    t["share_u15_pct"] = 100 * u15 / p25
    t["share_65plus_pct"] = 100 * o65 / p25
    t["cbr"] = 1000 * t.births_2025 / t.exposure_2025
    t["cdr"] = 1000 * t.deaths_2025 / t.exposure_2025
    t["nmr"] = 1000 * (t.arrivals_2025 - t.departures_2025) / t.exposure_2025
    return t


def ratios(ags, district):
    a = ags[ags.district_id == district]
    f = a.loc[a.sex == "F", "population_2025"].sum()
    m = a.loc[a.sex == "M", "population_2025"].sum()
    young = a.loc[a.age_start < 15, "population_2025"].sum()
    work = a.loc[(a.age_start >= 15) & (a.age_start < 65), "population_2025"].sum()
    old = a.loc[a.age_start >= 65, "population_2025"].sum()
    return {
        "district_id": district,
        "population_2025": int(f + m),
        "females": int(f), "males": int(m),
        "pop_0_14": int(young), "pop_15_64": int(work), "pop_65plus": int(old),
        "sex_ratio_males_per_100_females": 100 * m / f,
        "youth_dependency_ratio": 100 * young / work,
        "old_age_dependency_ratio": 100 * old / work,
        "total_dependency_ratio": 100 * (young + old) / work,
    }


def main(district_a="D13", district_b="D24", projection_district="D13"):
    print("Author: Mlungisi Ncube K (Population Structure Analyst)")
    print("PART 3: District selection, pyramids and ratios (Q1a)")
    d = load_raw()
    dist, ags = d["districts"], d["age_sex"]

    screen = district_screen(dist, ags)
    cols = ["region", "population_2025", "share_u15_pct", "share_65plus_pct", "cbr", "cdr", "nmr", "piped_water_pct"]
    show_table(screen[cols].sort_values("share_65plus_pct"), "Screening table used to choose the two districts", 1)
    save_table(screen.reset_index(), "p03_district_screen.csv")

    save_settings({"district_a": district_a, "district_b": district_b,
                   "projection_district": projection_district,
                   "reason": "Similar size (~173k), opposite age structures: D13 young/high fertility/"
                             "net out-migration; D24 old/natural decrease. D13 used for projection."})
    print(f"\nSelected districts: {district_a} and {district_b}; projection district: {projection_district}")

    # ---- Ratios ------------------------------------------------------------
    r = pd.DataFrame([ratios(ags, district_a), ratios(ags, district_b)])
    show_table(r.set_index("district_id").T, "Structure indicators at 1 January 2025", 2)
    save_table(r, "p03_structure_ratios.csv")

    # ---- Pyramids on a common scale ----------------------------------------
    pyr = (ags[ags.district_id.isin([district_a, district_b])]
           .pivot_table(index=["district_id", "age_start"], columns="sex", values="population_2025")
           .reset_index())
    pyr["age_group"] = pyr.age_start.map(age_label)
    save_table(pyr, "p03_pyramid_data.csv")

    xmax = np.ceil(pyr[["F", "M"]].to_numpy().max() / 2000) * 2000  # same limit for both panels
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.6), sharey=True)
    for ax, dname, colour in zip(axes, [district_a, district_b], [DARK, BLUE]):
        p = pyr[pyr.district_id == dname].sort_values("age_start")
        y = np.arange(len(p))
        ax.barh(y, -p.M, color=colour, label="Males", height=0.85)
        ax.barh(y, p.F, color=SKY, label="Females", height=0.85)
        ax.set_xlim(-xmax, xmax)
        ticks = np.arange(-xmax, xmax + 1, 2000)
        ax.set_xticks(ticks)
        ax.set_xticklabels([f"{abs(t) / 1000:.0f}" for t in ticks])
        ax.set_yticks(y)
        ax.set_yticklabels(p.age_group)
        ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=0.6)
        tot = int(p[["F", "M"]].to_numpy().sum())
        ax.set_title(f"District {dname} (total {tot:,} persons)")
        ax.set_xlabel("Population, thousands of persons (males left, females right)")
        ax.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Age group (years)")
    fig.suptitle(f"Population pyramids at 1 January 2025, common scale - {HYPO}", fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, "fig01_population_pyramids.png")

    a, b = r.iloc[0], r.iloc[1]
    print(f"\nInterpretation: {district_a} has a youth dependency ratio of {a.youth_dependency_ratio:.1f} "
          f"against {b.youth_dependency_ratio:.1f} in {district_b}, while the old-age ratio is "
          f"{a.old_age_dependency_ratio:.1f} vs {b.old_age_dependency_ratio:.1f}. Service pressure in "
          f"{district_a} is on schools and child health; in {district_b} it is on care of older people.")
    return screen, r


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ---- Code from src/part04_balance_and_rates_Gogodi_Vimbai.py ----
"""
Author: Gogodi Vimbai    |    Role: Demographic Rates Analyst    |    Checked by: Mlungisi Ncube K
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 4 - Population balance and demographic rates (Q1b).

Balancing equation for calendar 2025:
    P(1 Jan 2026) = P(1 Jan 2025) + Births - Deaths + Arrivals - Departures
P(1 Jan 2025) is the sum of age_sex.csv (README). Approximate mid-year exposure
is the mean of the two opening stocks, as the brief specifies.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import (load_raw, load_settings, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt,
                    DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE, HYPO)


def main():
    print("Author: Gogodi Vimbai (Demographic Rates Analyst)")
    print("PART 4: Population balance and crude rates (Q1b)")
    d = load_raw()
    dist, ags = d["districts"], d["age_sex"]
    s = load_settings()
    sel = [s["district_a"], s["district_b"]]

    t = dist.set_index("district_id").copy()
    t["population_2025"] = ags.groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum()
    print(f"Total baseline population, 1 Jan 2025 (all 24 districts): {int(t.population_2025.sum()):,}")
    print(f"Total reported population, 1 Jan 2026: {int(t.population_2026.sum()):,}")

    t["natural_increase"] = t.births_2025 - t.deaths_2025
    t["net_migration"] = t.arrivals_2025 - t.departures_2025
    t["reconstructed_2026"] = t.population_2025 + t.natural_increase + t.net_migration
    t["difference_reported_minus_reconstructed"] = t.population_2026 - t.reconstructed_2026
    t["exposure_2025"] = (t.population_2025 + t.population_2026) / 2
    t["CBR_per_1000"] = 1000 * t.births_2025 / t.exposure_2025
    t["CDR_per_1000"] = 1000 * t.deaths_2025 / t.exposure_2025
    t["RNI_per_1000"] = t.CBR_per_1000 - t.CDR_per_1000
    t["NMR_per_1000"] = 1000 * t.net_migration / t.exposure_2025
    t["growth_rate_per_1000"] = t.RNI_per_1000 + t.NMR_per_1000
    t["share_growth_from_migration_pct"] = 100 * t.net_migration / (t.population_2026 - t.population_2025)

    bal_cols = ["population_2025", "births_2025", "deaths_2025", "arrivals_2025", "departures_2025",
                "reconstructed_2026", "population_2026", "difference_reported_minus_reconstructed"]
    show_table(t.loc[sel, bal_cols].T, "Balancing equation, selected districts")
    tot = t[bal_cols].sum()
    show_table(tot.to_frame("All 24 districts"), "Balancing equation, all districts combined")
    print(f"Districts where the reconstruction differs from the report: "
          f"{int((t.difference_reported_minus_reconstructed != 0).sum())} of 24")

    rate_cols = ["exposure_2025", "CBR_per_1000", "CDR_per_1000", "RNI_per_1000", "NMR_per_1000", "growth_rate_per_1000"]
    show_table(t.loc[sel, rate_cols].T, "Crude rates per 1,000 residents, 2025", 2)
    save_table(t.reset_index(), "p04_balance_and_rates_all_districts.csv")

    # Chart: rates side by side
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.6))
    labels = ["Crude birth rate", "Crude death rate", "Natural increase", "Net migration rate"]
    keys = ["CBR_per_1000", "CDR_per_1000", "RNI_per_1000", "NMR_per_1000"]
    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    for i, (dn, c) in enumerate(zip(sel, [DARK, SKY])):
        vals = t.loc[dn, keys].to_numpy(float)
        bars = ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * 0.38, vals, 0.38, color=c, label=dn)
        for b_, v in zip(bars, vals):
            ax.text(b_.get_x() + b_.get_width() / 2, v + (0.4 if v >= 0 else -1.2), f"{v:.1f}",
                    ha="center", fontsize=7.5)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
    ax.set_ylabel("Rate per 1,000 residents (2025)")
    ax.set_title(f"Drivers of 2025 growth, {sel[0]} vs {sel[1]}")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    ax.text(0, -0.2, HYPO, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    save_fig(fig, "fig02_crude_rates.png")

    a, b = t.loc[sel[0]], t.loc[sel[1]]
    print(f"\n{sel[0]}: growth {a.growth_rate_per_1000:.1f} per 1,000 = natural increase {a.RNI_per_1000:.1f} "
          f"+ net migration {a.NMR_per_1000:.1f}.")
    print(f"{sel[1]}: growth {b.growth_rate_per_1000:.1f} per 1,000 = natural increase {b.RNI_per_1000:.1f} "
          f"+ net migration {b.NMR_per_1000:.1f}.")
    return t


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ---- Code from src/part05_life_table_Ketso_Thabiso_Mdlongwa.py ----
"""
Author: Ketso Thabiso Mdlongwa    |    Role: Mortality and Life-Table Analyst    |    Checked by: Emeldah Munyanyi
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 5 - Abridged life table from the separate mortality schedule (Q1c).

    m_x  = deaths / person_years
    q_x  = n m_x / (1 + (n - a_x) m_x)          (q_85+ = 1)
    l_0  = 100,000 ; d_x = l_x q_x ; l_{x+n} = l_x - d_x
    L_x  = n l_{x+n} + a_x d_x                    (L_85+ = l_85 / m_85+)
    T_x  = sum of L from x upwards ; e_x = T_x / l_x
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import load_raw, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt, DARK, BLUE, HYPO, RADIX, age_label


def build_life_table(life: pd.DataFrame, radix: int = RADIX) -> pd.DataFrame:
    lt = life.copy().sort_values("age_start").reset_index(drop=True)
    lt["age_group"] = lt.age_start.map(age_label)
    lt["n"] = lt.interval_years
    lt["mx"] = lt.deaths / lt.person_years
    lt["qx"] = lt.n * lt.mx / (1 + (lt.n - lt.ax) * lt.mx)
    last = lt.index[-1]
    lt.loc[last, "qx"] = 1.0                        # open interval: everyone dies eventually
    lx = [float(radix)]
    for q in lt.qx.iloc[:-1]:
        lx.append(lx[-1] * (1 - q))
    lt["lx"] = lx
    lt["dx"] = lt.lx * lt.qx
    lt["l_next"] = lt.lx.shift(-1).fillna(0.0)
    lt["Lx"] = lt.n * lt.l_next + lt.ax * lt.dx
    lt.loc[last, "Lx"] = lt.loc[last, "lx"] / lt.loc[last, "mx"]
    lt["Tx"] = lt.Lx[::-1].cumsum()[::-1]
    lt["ex"] = lt.Tx / lt.lx
    return lt


def main():
    print("Author: Ketso Thabiso Mdlongwa (Mortality and Life-Table Analyst)")
    print("PART 5: Abridged life table (Q1c)")
    life = load_raw()["life"]
    lt = build_life_table(life)
    out = lt[["age_group", "n", "ax", "mx", "qx", "lx", "dx", "Lx", "Tx", "ex"]]
    show_table(out.round({"mx": 5, "qx": 5, "lx": 0, "dx": 0, "Lx": 0, "Tx": 0, "ex": 2}),
               "Abridged life table (radix 100,000)")
    save_table(out, "p05_life_table.csv")

    e0 = lt.loc[0, "ex"]
    e65 = lt.loc[lt.age_start == 65, "ex"].iloc[0]
    print(f"\nLife expectancy at birth e0 = {e0:.2f} years; at age 65 e65 = {e65:.2f} years")

    # ---- Numerical checks ----------------------------------------------------
    checks = pd.DataFrame([
        {"check": "Sum of d_x equals the radix", "value": lt.dx.sum(), "target": RADIX},
        {"check": "T_0 equals the sum of all L_x", "value": lt.Tx.iloc[0], "target": lt.Lx.sum()},
        {"check": "e_85+ equals 1 / m_85+", "value": lt.ex.iloc[-1], "target": 1 / lt.mx.iloc[-1]},
        {"check": "l_5 = l_0 x (1 - q_0)", "value": lt.lx.iloc[1], "target": RADIX * (1 - lt.qx.iloc[0])},
        {"check": "Manual q_0 = 5(0.008)/(1+(5-1.2)(0.008))", "value": lt.qx.iloc[0],
         "target": 5 * 0.008 / (1 + 3.8 * 0.008)},
    ])
    checks["abs_difference"] = (checks.value - checks.target).abs()
    checks["passed"] = checks.abs_difference < 1e-6
    show_table(checks, "Life-table checks")
    save_table(checks, "p05_life_table_checks.csv")

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
    ax1.plot(lt.age_start, lt.lx, marker="o", color=DARK, label="l(x) survivors")
    ax1.set_xlabel("Exact age x (years)")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Survivors l(x) out of 100,000 births")
    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(lt.age_start, lt.ex, marker="s", color=BLUE, ls="--", label="e(x) years")
    ax2.set_ylabel("Life expectancy e(x), years")
    ax1.set_title(f"Survivorship and life expectancy (e0 = {e0:.1f}, e65 = {e65:.1f})")
    h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax1.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, frameon=False, loc="lower left")
    ax1.text(0, -0.22, HYPO, transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    save_fig(fig, "fig03_life_table.png")
    return lt


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ---- Code from src/part06_growth_and_cohort_component_Stuart_Gavera.py ----
"""
Author: Stuart Gavera    |    Role: Population Projection Modeller    |    Checked by: Taonashe Amanda Kuipa
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 6 - Arithmetic, geometric and cohort-component projections (Q2a, Q2b).

Projection district and period: selected district, 1 Jan 2025 -> 1 Jan 2030.

Timing assumptions for the cohort-component model (documented as the brief asks):
  * Survival: each 1 Jan 2025 cohort moves up one 5-year band with its supplied
    survival_5yr. Ages 80-84 survivors and 85+ survivors (retention) form 85+.
  * Births: 5 x (2025 births to women) x fertility multiplier, split 49% F /
    51% M, then multiplied by the scenario newborn survival and placed in 0-4.
  * Migration: 5 x each 2025 flow x scenario multiplier, added (arrivals) or
    removed (departures) at the END of the period by destination age and sex,
    including 0-4. Migrants are therefore not exposed to mortality or
    fertility inside the period (end-of-period adjustment).
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import (load_raw, load_settings, show_table, save_table, HYPO, age_label,
                    FEMALE_BIRTH_SHARE, MALE_BIRTH_SHARE)


def growth_models(p2020: float, p2025: float, years: int = 5):
    """Arithmetic and geometric growth fitted to two opening counts."""
    slope = (p2025 - p2020) / years                       # persons per year
    r_arith = slope / p2020                               # constant absolute increase, as a rate of P2020
    r_geom = (p2025 / p2020) ** (1 / years) - 1           # constant compound annual rate
    return {
        "P2020_reported": p2020,
        "P2025_sum_of_age_sex": p2025,
        "arithmetic_increase_per_year": slope,
        "arithmetic_rate_per_year": r_arith,
        "geometric_rate_per_year": r_geom,
        "arithmetic_P2030": p2025 + slope * years,
        "geometric_P2030": p2025 * (1 + r_geom) ** years,
    }


def cohort_component(base: pd.DataFrame, scen_row: pd.Series, fert_override: float | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Five-year projection for one district. `base` is that district's 36 age-sex rows."""
    fert = scen_row.fertility_multiplier if fert_override is None else fert_override
    births_2025 = base.loc[base.sex == "F", "births_to_women_2025"].sum()
    births_5yr = 5 * births_2025 * fert
    out = []
    for sex, share, nb in [("F", FEMALE_BIRTH_SHARE, scen_row.newborn_survival_f),
                           ("M", MALE_BIRTH_SHARE, scen_row.newborn_survival_m)]:
        b = base[base.sex == sex].sort_values("age_start")
        p = b.population_2025.to_numpy(float)
        s = b.survival_5yr.to_numpy(float)
        survived = np.zeros(18)
        survived[1:17] = p[0:16] * s[0:16]                  # 0-4 -> 5-9, ..., 75-79 -> 80-84
        survived[17] = p[16] * s[16] + p[17] * s[17]        # 80-84 -> 85+ plus 85+ retained
        births_sex = births_5yr * share
        surviving_births = np.zeros(18)
        surviving_births[0] = births_sex * nb
        arr = 5 * b.arrivals_2025.to_numpy(float) * scen_row.arrivals_multiplier
        dep = 5 * b.departures_2025.to_numpy(float) * scen_row.departures_multiplier
        pop2030 = survived + surviving_births + arr - dep
        out.append(pd.DataFrame({
            "sex": sex, "age_start": b.age_start.to_numpy(),
            "pop_2025": p, "survival_5yr": s,
            "survivors_2030": survived,
            "births_5yr": np.where(b.age_start == 0, births_sex, 0.0),
            "surviving_births": surviving_births,
            "arrivals_5yr": arr, "departures_5yr": dep,
            "net_migration_5yr": arr - dep,
            "pop_2030": pop2030,
        }))
    res = pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)
    res["age_group"] = res.age_start.map(age_label)
    return res


def accounting(res: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Totals and the accounting identity P2030 = P2025 - deaths + surviving births + net migration."""
    p25 = res.pop_2025.sum()
    surv = res.survivors_2030.sum()
    deaths_cohort = p25 - surv
    births = res.births_5yr.sum()
    sb = res.surviving_births.sum()
    nm = res.net_migration_5yr.sum()
    p30 = res.pop_2030.sum()
    identity = p25 - deaths_cohort + sb + nm
    return {
        "P2025": p25, "deaths_baseline_cohorts": deaths_cohort, "births_5yr": births,
        "deaths_among_births": births - sb, "surviving_births": sb,
        "arrivals_5yr": res.arrivals_5yr.sum(), "departures_5yr": res.departures_5yr.sum(),
        "net_migration_5yr": nm, "P2030": p30,
        "identity_check_gap": p30 - identity,
        "negative_cells": int((res.pop_2030 < 0).sum()),
        "P2030_females": res.loc[res.sex == "F", "pop_2030"].sum(),
        "P2030_males": res.loc[res.sex == "M", "pop_2030"].sum(),
        "share_u15_pct": 100 * res.loc[res.age_start < 15, "pop_2030"].sum() / p30,
        "share_65plus_pct": 100 * res.loc[res.age_start >= 65, "pop_2030"].sum() / p30,
        "pop_0_4": res.loc[res.age_start == 0, "pop_2030"].sum(),
    }


def main():
    s = load_settings()
    dname = s["projection_district"]
    print("Author: Stuart Gavera (Population Projection Modeller)")
    print(f"PART 6: Growth models and cohort-component projection for {dname} (Q2a, Q2b)")
    d = load_raw()
    dist, ags, scen = d["districts"], d["age_sex"], d["scen"]
    base = ags[ags.district_id == dname]

    # ---- Q2a arithmetic and geometric -------------------------------------
    p2020 = float(dist.loc[dist.district_id == dname, "population_2020"].iloc[0])
    p2025 = float(base.population_2025.sum())
    gm = growth_models(p2020, p2025)
    show_table(pd.Series(gm).to_frame(dname), "Arithmetic and geometric growth, 2020-2025 fit")
    save_table(pd.DataFrame([{"district_id": dname, **gm}]), "p06_growth_models.csv")
    print("Inputs that are estimates: P2020 (reported opening stock) and P2025 (sum of the age-sex "
          "estimates). The 2030 totals are conditional projections: they hold only if the 2020-25 "
          "pattern of change continues unchanged.")

    # ---- Q2b cohort-component, three scenarios ---------------------------
    all_res, summ = [], []
    for _, row in scen.iterrows():
        res = cohort_component(base, row)
        res.insert(0, "scenario", row.scenario)
        res.insert(0, "district_id", dname)
        all_res.append(res)
        acc = accounting(res)
        summ.append({"scenario": row.scenario, **acc})
    detail = pd.concat(all_res, ignore_index=True)
    summary = pd.DataFrame(summ).set_index("scenario").loc[["Low", "Base", "High"]]
    save_table(detail, "p06_cohort_component_detail.csv")
    save_table(summary.reset_index(), "p06_cohort_component_summary.csv")

    show_table(summary[["P2025", "deaths_baseline_cohorts", "births_5yr", "deaths_among_births",
                        "net_migration_5yr", "P2030", "identity_check_gap", "negative_cells"]].T,
               "Cohort-component accounting by scenario", 1)
    assert summary.identity_check_gap.abs().max() < 1e-6, "accounting identity failed"
    assert summary.negative_cells.max() == 0, "negative population cell"
    # Check: survivors computed band by band equal the total
    base_res = detail[detail.scenario == "Base"]
    check_85 = base_res.query("age_start == 85").survivors_2030.sum()
    manual_85 = sum(r.population_2025 * r.survival_5yr for r in base.itertuples() if r.age_start >= 80)
    print(f"85+ survivors check: model {check_85:,.2f} vs manual {manual_85:,.2f}")
    print("All accounting checks passed: identity gap = 0, no negative cells.")

    wide = detail.pivot_table(index=["age_start", "age_group", "sex"], columns="scenario",
                              values="pop_2030").reset_index()[["age_group", "sex", "Low", "Base", "High"]]
    show_table(wide.round(0), f"Projected population on 1 Jan 2030 by age and sex, {dname}")
    return gm, detail, summary


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ---- Code from src/part07_projection_comparison_Taonashe_Amanda_Kuipa.py ----
"""
Author: Taonashe Amanda Kuipa    |    Role: Scenario and Sensitivity Analyst    |    Checked by: Stuart Gavera
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 7 - Comparison of projections and fertility sensitivity (Q2c).

  * Compare cohort-component totals (Low, Base, High) with arithmetic and
    geometric totals for 1 Jan 2030.
  * Report shares under 15 and 65+.
  * Sensitivity: start from Base and change ONLY the fertility multiplier to the
    High value (1.12). Measure the effect on ages 0-4.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from common import (load_raw, load_settings, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt,
                    DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE, GREY, HYPO, age_label)
from part06_growth_and_cohort_component_Stuart_Gavera import growth_models, cohort_component, accounting


def main():
    s = load_settings()
    dname = s["projection_district"]
    print("Author: Taonashe Amanda Kuipa (Scenario and Sensitivity Analyst)")
    print(f"PART 7: Projection comparison and sensitivity for {dname} (Q2c)")
    d = load_raw()
    dist, ags, scen = d["districts"], d["age_sex"], d["scen"]
    base = ags[ags.district_id == dname]
    scen_i = scen.set_index("scenario")

    p2020 = float(dist.loc[dist.district_id == dname, "population_2020"].iloc[0])
    p2025 = float(base.population_2025.sum())
    gm = growth_models(p2020, p2025)

    rows = [{"method": "Baseline 1 Jan 2025", "P2030": p2025,
             "share_u15_pct": 100 * base.loc[base.age_start < 15, "population_2025"].sum() / p2025,
             "share_65plus_pct": 100 * base.loc[base.age_start >= 65, "population_2025"].sum() / p2025},
            {"method": "Arithmetic", "P2030": gm["arithmetic_P2030"], "share_u15_pct": np.nan, "share_65plus_pct": np.nan},
            {"method": "Geometric", "P2030": gm["geometric_P2030"], "share_u15_pct": np.nan, "share_65plus_pct": np.nan}]
    results = {}
    for sc in ["Low", "Base", "High"]:
        res = cohort_component(base, scen_i.loc[sc])
        acc = accounting(res)
        results[sc] = res
        rows.append({"method": f"Cohort-component {sc}", "P2030": acc["P2030"],
                     "share_u15_pct": acc["share_u15_pct"], "share_65plus_pct": acc["share_65plus_pct"]})
    comp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    comp["change_from_2025"] = comp.P2030 - p2025
    comp["pct_change_from_2025"] = 100 * comp.change_from_2025 / p2025
    comp["difference_vs_CC_Base"] = comp.P2030 - comp.loc[comp.method == "Cohort-component Base", "P2030"].iloc[0]
    show_table(comp, "Projected totals for 1 Jan 2030 and age shares", 2)
    save_table(comp, "p07_projection_comparison.csv")

    # ---- Sensitivity: Base with High fertility -----------------------------
    base_row = scen_i.loc["Base"]
    sens = cohort_component(base, base_row, fert_override=scen_i.loc["High", "fertility_multiplier"])
    b04 = results["Base"].query("age_start == 0").groupby("sex").pop_2030.sum()
    s04 = sens.query("age_start == 0").groupby("sex").pop_2030.sum()
    sens_tab = pd.DataFrame({"Base": b04, "Base + High fertility": s04})
    sens_tab.loc["Total"] = sens_tab.sum()
    sens_tab["change"] = sens_tab["Base + High fertility"] - sens_tab["Base"]
    sens_tab["pct_change"] = 100 * sens_tab.change / sens_tab.Base
    show_table(sens_tab, "Sensitivity: ages 0-4 on 1 Jan 2030 (only fertility changed)", 1)
    save_table(sens_tab.reset_index(), "p07_fertility_sensitivity.csv")
    acc_s = accounting(sens)
    print(f"Total population changes from {accounting(results['Base'])['P2030']:,.0f} to {acc_s['P2030']:,.0f}; "
          f"share under 15 from {accounting(results['Base'])['share_u15_pct']:.2f}% to {acc_s['share_u15_pct']:.2f}%.")

    # ---- Charts ------------------------------------------------------------
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.4))
    cmp = comp[comp.method != "Baseline 1 Jan 2025"]
    colours = [GREY, GREY, SKY, BLUE, DARK]
    bars = ax.bar(cmp.method.str.replace("Cohort-component ", "CC "), cmp.P2030, color=colours)
    ax.axhline(p2025, color=ORANGE, ls="--", lw=1, label=f"1 Jan 2025 baseline ({p2025:,.0f})")
    for b_, v in zip(bars, cmp.P2030):
        ax.text(b_.get_x() + b_.get_width() / 2, v + 600, f"{v:,.0f}", ha="center", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylim(p2025 * 0.9, cmp.P2030.max() * 1.03)
    ax.set_ylabel("Projected population, persons (1 Jan 2030)")
    ax.set_title(f"{dname}: total population on 1 January 2030 by method")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
    ax.text(0, -0.2, HYPO, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    save_fig(fig, "fig04_projection_comparison.png")

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
    ages = results["Base"].query("sex == 'F'").age_start.to_numpy()
    tot25 = base.groupby("age_start").population_2025.sum().reindex(ages).to_numpy()
    ax.plot(ages, tot25 / 1000, color=GREY, marker="o", ms=3, label="1 Jan 2025 (baseline)")
    for sc, c in zip(["Low", "Base", "High"], [SKY, BLUE, DARK]):
        y = results[sc].groupby("age_start").pop_2030.sum().reindex(ages).to_numpy()
        ax.plot(ages, y / 1000, color=c, marker="o", ms=3, label=f"1 Jan 2030 {sc}")
    ax.set_xticks(ages)
    ax.set_xticklabels([age_label(a) for a in ages], rotation=60, fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("Population, thousands of persons")
    ax.set_xlabel("Age group (years)")
    ax.set_title(f"{dname}: age distribution, baseline and projected scenarios")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    ax.text(0, -0.32, HYPO, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    save_fig(fig, "fig05_projection_age_profile.png")

    # Long table for Power BI (one row per scenario-age-sex)
    pbi = []
    for sc, res in list(results.items()) + [("Base + High fertility", sens)]:
        r = res[["sex", "age_start", "age_group", "pop_2025", "survivors_2030", "surviving_births",
                 "net_migration_5yr", "pop_2030"]].copy()
        r.insert(0, "scenario", sc)
        r.insert(0, "district_id", dname)
        pbi.append(r)
    pbi = pd.concat(pbi, ignore_index=True)
    pbi["scenario_order"] = pbi.scenario.map({"Low": 1, "Base": 2, "High": 3, "Base + High fertility": 4})
    save_table(pbi, "pbi_projection_by_age_sex.csv")
    return comp, sens_tab


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Comparison. The trend models (189–191 thousand) sit above even the High cohort-component scenario because 2020–25 growth averaged about 1.8% a year, while the 2025 components imply much slower growth. The cohort-component model also keeps the under-15 share near 29% and lets the 65+ share fall slightly.

Sensitivity. Raising only the Base fertility multiplier to 1.12 adds about 2,290 children aged 0–4 (+12%). Planning implication: early-childhood and primary-school places in D13 should be planned for the higher range. Limitation: births are tied to the 2025 female age structure and migrants do not have births inside the period.

# ---- Code from src/part08_markov_model_Hillary_Zivuku.py ----
"""
Author: Hillary Zivuku    |    Role: Actuarial Modeller (Markov Model)    |    Checked by: Shaun Kanojerera
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 8 - Three-state continuous-time Markov model for the insured cohort (Q3a-Q3d).

States: H (healthy), I (ill), D (dead, absorbing). Recovery I -> H is allowed.
Pooling rule from the README: exposure_py and initial_lives are repeated across
the two destinations of each district-origin, so we keep ONE copy per
district-origin before summing. Transition counts are summed over all rows.

    mu_ij = (sum of observed i->j jumps) / (pooled exposure in origin state i)
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.linalg import expm

from common import (load_raw, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt, DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE,
                    GREY, HYPO, BENEFIT_USD, ILL_DEATH_MULTIPLIER)
from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrowPatch, Circle

STATES = ["H", "I", "D"]
NAMES = {"H": "Healthy", "I": "Ill", "D": "Dead"}


def estimate_generator(ins: pd.DataFrame):
    exposure = (ins.drop_duplicates(["district_id", "origin"])      # one copy per district-origin
                .groupby("origin").exposure_py.sum())
    counts = ins.groupby(["origin", "destination"]).transition_count.sum()
    rows = []
    for (o, dst), n in counts.items():
        rows.append({"origin": o, "destination": dst, "pooled_jumps": int(n),
                     "pooled_exposure_py": float(exposure[o]), "intensity": n / exposure[o]})
    est = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    mu = {(r.origin, r.destination): r.intensity for r in est.itertuples()}
    Q = np.zeros((3, 3))
    Q[0, 1], Q[0, 2] = mu[("H", "I")], mu[("H", "D")]
    Q[1, 0], Q[1, 2] = mu[("I", "H")], mu[("I", "D")]
    for i in range(3):
        Q[i, i] = -Q[i].sum()
    return est, Q


def draw_state_diagram(Q, path_name):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.2))
    pos = {"H": (0.1, 0.72), "I": (0.9, 0.72), "D": (0.5, 0.1)}
    cols = {"H": BLUE, "I": ORANGE, "D": GREY}
    for st, (x, y) in pos.items():
        ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), 0.095, color=cols[st], alpha=0.95, zorder=3))
        ax.text(x, y, f"{st}\n{NAMES[st]}", ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=9,
                fontweight="bold", zorder=4)

    def arrow(a, b, label, rad, off):
        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = pos[a], pos[b]
        ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x1, y1), (x2, y2), connectionstyle=f"arc3,rad={rad}",
                                     arrowstyle="-|>", mutation_scale=16, lw=1.6, color=DARK,
                                     shrinkA=24, shrinkB=24, zorder=2))
        ax.text((x1 + x2) / 2 + off[0], (y1 + y2) / 2 + off[1], label, ha="center", fontsize=8.5,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.2", fc="white", ec="none"))

    arrow("H", "I", f"onset  mu_HI = {Q[0, 1]:.4f}", -0.2, (0, 0.12))
    arrow("I", "H", f"recovery  mu_IH = {Q[1, 0]:.4f}", -0.2, (0, -0.15))
    arrow("H", "D", f"death  mu_HD = {Q[0, 2]:.4f}", 0.0, (-0.2, -0.02))
    arrow("I", "D", f"death  mu_ID = {Q[1, 2]:.4f}", 0.0, (0.2, -0.02))
    ax.text(0.5, -0.04, "D is absorbing (no exits). Intensities per person-year, pooled over 24 districts.",
            ha="center", fontsize=7.5, color="black")
    ax.text(0.5, -0.11, HYPO, ha="center", fontsize=7, color="grey")
    ax.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.14, 0.92)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")
    ax.set_title("Healthy-ill-dead model with recovery")
    save_fig(fig, path_name)


def main():
    print("Author: Hillary Zivuku (Actuarial Modeller (Markov Model))")
    print("PART 8: Three-state continuous-time Markov model (Q3)")
    ins = load_raw()["ins"]

    # ---- 3a generator -----------------------------------------------------
    est, Q = estimate_generator(ins)
    if ILL_DEATH_MULTIPLIER != 1.0:
        # What-if run: scale mu_ID and rebuild the diagonal so rows still sum to zero
        Q[1, 2] *= ILL_DEATH_MULTIPLIER
        Q[1, 1] = -(Q[1, 0] + Q[1, 2])
        print(f"WHAT-IF: I->D intensity multiplied by {ILL_DEATH_MULTIPLIER} -> mu_ID = {Q[1, 2]:.4f}")
    show_table(est, "Pooled jumps, exposure and transition intensities")
    save_table(est, "p08_transition_intensities.csv")
    Qdf = pd.DataFrame(Q, index=STATES, columns=STATES)
    show_table(Qdf, "Generator matrix Q (order H, I, D)", 6)
    save_table(Qdf.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "from_state"}), "p08_generator_Q.csv")
    off = Q[~np.eye(3, dtype=bool)]
    print(f"Row sums of Q: {np.round(Q.sum(axis=1), 12)}  -> all zero: {np.allclose(Q.sum(axis=1), 0)}")
    print(f"Off-diagonal entries non-negative: {(off >= 0).all()}; diagonal non-positive: {(np.diag(Q) <= 0).all()}")
    draw_state_diagram(Q, "fig06_markov_state_diagram.png")

    # ---- 3b holding times and jump chain -------------------------------------
    hold = pd.DataFrame({"state": ["H", "I"], "total_exit_intensity": [-Q[0, 0], -Q[1, 1]],
                         "mean_holding_time_years": [1 / -Q[0, 0], 1 / -Q[1, 1]]})
    show_table(hold, "Mean holding times in the living states", 4)
    q_i = -Q[1, 1]
    jump = pd.DataFrame({"from": ["I", "I"], "next_state": ["H (recovery)", "D (death)"],
                         "probability": [Q[1, 0] / q_i, Q[1, 2] / q_i]})
    show_table(jump, "Next-jump destinations from the ill state", 4)
    save_table(pd.concat([hold, jump], axis=1), "p08_holding_and_jump.csv")

    # ---- 3c transition matrices --------------------------------------------
    P1, P2 = expm(Q * 1.0), expm(Q * 2.0)
    for name, P in [("P(1)", P1), ("P(2)", P2)]:
        show_table(pd.DataFrame(P, index=STATES, columns=STATES), f"Transition probability matrix {name}", 6)
    checks = pd.DataFrame([
        {"check": "P(1) entries non-negative", "result": bool((P1 >= -1e-12).all())},
        {"check": "P(2) entries non-negative", "result": bool((P2 >= -1e-12).all())},
        {"check": "P(1) rows sum to 1", "result": bool(np.allclose(P1.sum(1), 1, atol=1e-12))},
        {"check": "P(2) rows sum to 1", "result": bool(np.allclose(P2.sum(1), 1, atol=1e-12))},
        {"check": "Death absorbing: row D of P(1), P(2) = (0,0,1)",
         "result": bool(np.allclose(P1[2], [0, 0, 1]) and np.allclose(P2[2], [0, 0, 1]))},
        {"check": "P(2) = P(1) @ P(1) (Chapman-Kolmogorov)",
         "result": bool(np.allclose(P2, P1 @ P1, atol=1e-12)),
         "max_abs_diff": float(np.abs(P2 - P1 @ P1).max())},
    ])
    show_table(checks, "Probability checks")
    save_table(checks, "p08_probability_checks.csv")
    print(f"\nNext-jump recovery probability from I = {jump.probability.iloc[0]:.4f}, but "
          f"P_IH(1) = {P1[1, 0]:.4f}. The jump probability ignores timing (it is where the next move "
          f"goes, whenever it happens), while P_IH(1) is the chance of being healthy exactly at t = 1: "
          f"some ill lives have not moved yet, and some recover and fall ill again or die within the year.")

    tm = []
    for t, P in [(1, P1), (2, P2)]:
        for i, a in enumerate(STATES):
            for j, b in enumerate(STATES):
                tm.append({"t_years": t, "from_state": a, "to_state": b, "probability": P[i, j]})
    tm = pd.DataFrame(tm)
    order = {"H": 1, "I": 2, "D": 3}
    tm["from_order"], tm["to_order"] = tm.from_state.map(order), tm.to_state.map(order)
    save_table(tm, "pbi_markov_transition_matrices.csv")

    # Initial pooled counts (once per district-origin)
    init_by_d = (ins.drop_duplicates(["district_id", "origin"])
                 .pivot(index="district_id", columns="origin", values="initial_lives"))
    init_by_d["D"] = 0
    n0 = init_by_d[STATES].sum().to_numpy(float)
    occ = pd.DataFrame([n0, n0 @ P1, n0 @ P2], columns=STATES, index=["t=0", "t=1", "t=2"])
    occ["total"] = occ.sum(axis=1)
    show_table(occ, "Expected occupancy of the pooled insured cohort", 1)
    save_table(occ.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "time"}), "p08_expected_occupancy.csv")

    # ---- 3d benefits ---------------------------------------------------------
    deaths_y1 = occ.loc["t=1", "D"] - occ.loc["t=0", "D"]
    deaths_y2 = occ.loc["t=2", "D"] - occ.loc["t=1", "D"]
    claims = pd.DataFrame({"year": ["Year 1 (0-1)", "Year 2 (1-2)", "Two years"],
                           "expected_deaths": [deaths_y1, deaths_y2, deaths_y1 + deaths_y2]})
    claims["expected_benefits_usd"] = claims.expected_deaths * BENEFIT_USD
    show_table(claims, "Expected covered deaths and benefit payments (USD 1,000 per death, undiscounted)", 2)
    save_table(claims, "p08_expected_claims.csv")

    # District split for the dashboard: pooled Q applied to each district's initial lives
    rows = []
    for dist_id, r in init_by_d.iterrows():
        v0 = r[STATES].to_numpy(float)
        v1, v2 = v0 @ P1, v0 @ P2
        for t, v in [(0, v0), (1, v1), (2, v2)]:
            for st, val in zip(STATES, v):
                rows.append({"district_id": dist_id, "t_years": t, "state": NAMES[st], "expected_lives": val})
        rows_claim = [(1, v1[2] - v0[2]), (2, v2[2] - v1[2])]
        for yr, dth in rows_claim:
            rows.append({"district_id": dist_id, "t_years": yr, "state": f"Claims year {yr}",
                         "expected_lives": dth})
    dshare = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    occ_long = dshare[~dshare.state.str.startswith("Claims")].copy()
    occ_long["state_order"] = occ_long.state.map({"Healthy": 1, "Ill": 2, "Dead": 3})
    save_table(occ_long, "pbi_markov_occupancy_by_district.csv")
    cl = dshare[dshare.state.str.startswith("Claims")].rename(columns={"expected_lives": "expected_deaths",
                                                                       "t_years": "policy_year"})
    cl["expected_benefits_usd"] = cl.expected_deaths * BENEFIT_USD
    save_table(cl.drop(columns="state"), "pbi_expected_claims_by_district.csv")
    print(f"District split reconciles to pooled claims: year 1 {cl[cl.policy_year == 1].expected_benefits_usd.sum():,.2f} "
          f"vs {claims.expected_benefits_usd.iloc[0]:,.2f}")

    # Occupancy chart over 0-5 years
    ts = np.linspace(0, 5, 51)
    path = np.array([n0 @ expm(Q * t) for t in ts])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.3))
    for k, (st, c) in enumerate(zip(STATES, [BLUE, ORANGE, GREY])):
        ax.plot(ts, path[:, k], color=c, lw=2, label=NAMES[st])
    for t in (1, 2):
        ax.axvline(t, color="black", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Years from the start of cover")
    ax.set_ylabel("Expected number of lives")
    ax.set_title("Expected occupancy of the pooled insured cohort, n(t) = n(0) P(t)")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    ax.text(0, -0.22, HYPO, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    save_fig(fig, "fig07_markov_occupancy.png")
    return Q, P1, P2, occ, claims


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Why the two probabilities differ. The next-jump probability of recovery (0.785) says where an ill life goes next, whenever that move happens. P_IH(1) (0.198) is the chance of being healthy exactly one year later: many ill lives have not moved yet (mean holding time 3.2 years), and some recover and fall ill again, or die, within the year.

Limitation of pooling. One set of constant intensities assumes every district, age group and policy duration shares the same risks over time. Districts differ, and the hazard of death rises with age and illness duration, so the expected claims are an average that may misstate a particular district's or a particular year's cost.

# ---- Code from src/part09_clustering_features_Shaun_Kanojerera.py ----
"""
Author: Shaun Kanojerera    |    Role: Feature Engineering Analyst    |    Checked by: Hillary Zivuku
HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 9 - District feature table for clustering (Q4a).

Features (one row per district, all 24 districts):
  share_u15_pct     share of 1 Jan 2025 population aged 0-14 (%)
  share_65plus_pct  share aged 65+ (%)
  nmr_per_1000      2025 net migration rate per 1,000 (mid-year exposure from Part 4)
  piped_water_pct   household piped-water access (%)

Imputation rule (primary fit): k-nearest-neighbour imputation with k = 3. For a
district with missing water we find the 3 districts closest to it on the three
complete, standardised features and use the mean of their water values.
Why: in the 22 complete districts water access moves strongly with the
migration and age profile (see the correlations printed below), so neighbours
with the same profile give a more realistic value than one overall median,
which would place both districts in the middle of the range.
Sensitivity (Part 10): overall median imputation.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from common import load_raw, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt, DARK, BLUE, SKY, HYPO

FEATURES = ["share_u15_pct", "share_65plus_pct", "nmr_per_1000", "piped_water_pct"]


def build_features(dist, ags):
    t = dist.set_index("district_id").copy()
    p25 = ags.groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum()
    t["share_u15_pct"] = 100 * ags[ags.age_start < 15].groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum() / p25
    t["share_65plus_pct"] = 100 * ags[ags.age_start >= 65].groupby("district_id").population_2025.sum() / p25
    expo = (p25 + t.population_2026) / 2
    t["nmr_per_1000"] = 1000 * (t.arrivals_2025 - t.departures_2025) / expo
    return t[["region"] + FEATURES].copy()


def knn_impute(feat: pd.DataFrame, target="piped_water_pct", k=3):
    base_cols = [c for c in FEATURES if c != target]
    z = (feat[base_cols] - feat[base_cols].mean()) / feat[base_cols].std(ddof=0)
    out = feat[target].copy()
    notes = []
    for d_id in feat.index[feat[target].isna()]:
        dist = np.sqrt(((z.loc[feat[target].notna()] - z.loc[d_id]) ** 2).sum(axis=1)).sort_values()
        nb = dist.index[:k]
        out[d_id] = feat.loc[nb, target].mean()
        notes.append({"district_id": d_id, "neighbours": ", ".join(nb),
                      "neighbour_water_values": ", ".join(f"{v:.1f}" for v in feat.loc[nb, target]),
                      "imputed_knn": out[d_id],
                      "overall_median_alternative": feat[target].median(),
                      "region_median_alternative": feat.loc[feat.region == feat.loc[d_id, "region"], target].median()})
    return out, pd.DataFrame(notes)


def main():
    print("Author: Shaun Kanojerera (Feature Engineering Analyst)")
    print("PART 9: Clustering feature table, imputation, outliers, standardisation (Q4a)")
    d = load_raw()
    feat = build_features(d["districts"], d["age_sex"])

    print("Correlation of water access with the other features (22 complete districts):")
    print(feat[FEATURES].dropna().corr()["piped_water_pct"].round(3).to_string())

    feat["piped_water_imputed_flag"] = feat.piped_water_pct.isna().astype(int)
    feat["piped_water_raw"] = feat.piped_water_pct
    feat["piped_water_pct"], notes = knn_impute(feat)
    show_table(notes, "Imputation of the two missing water values (k = 3 nearest neighbours)", 2)
    save_table(notes, "p09_imputation_notes.csv")

    # ---- Outlier check ------------------------------------------------------
    rows = []
    for c in FEATURES:
        x = feat[c]
        q1, q3 = x.quantile([0.25, 0.75])
        iqr = q3 - q1
        z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std(ddof=0)
        rows.append({"feature": c, "mean": x.mean(), "sd": x.std(ddof=0), "min": x.min(), "max": x.max(),
                     "max_abs_z": z.abs().max(),
                     "iqr_outliers": ", ".join(x.index[(x < q1 - 1.5 * iqr) | (x > q3 + 1.5 * iqr)]) or "none",
                     "z_above_3": ", ".join(x.index[z.abs() > 3]) or "none"})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    show_table(out, "Outlier check (IQR rule and |z| > 3)", 2)
    save_table(out, "p09_outlier_check.csv")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(10, 2.8))
    labels = ["Under 15 (%)", "65+ (%)", "Net migration per 1,000", "Piped water (%)"]
    for ax, c, lab in zip(axes, FEATURES, labels):
        ax.boxplot(feat[c], widths=0.5, patch_artist=True, boxprops=dict(facecolor=SKY, color=DARK),
                   medianprops=dict(color=DARK))
        ax.scatter(np.random.default_rng(1).normal(1, 0.04, len(feat)), feat[c], s=10, color=DARK, zorder=3)
        ax.set_title(lab, fontsize=8.5)
        ax.set_xticks([])
    fig.suptitle(f"Distribution of clustering features across 24 districts - {HYPO}", fontsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, "fig08_feature_boxplots.png")

    # ---- Standardise --------------------------------------------------------
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    Z = pd.DataFrame(scaler.fit_transform(feat[FEATURES]), index=feat.index, columns=[f"z_{c}" for c in FEATURES])
    print("\nAfter standardising: means", Z.mean().round(10).tolist(), "sds", Z.std(ddof=0).round(6).tolist())
    print("district_id is excluded from the features: it is only a label. Its order (D01...D24) has no "
          "numerical meaning, so using it would create false distances between districts.")
    table = feat.join(Z)
    save_table(table.reset_index(), "p09_cluster_features.csv")
    show_table(table[FEATURES + ["piped_water_imputed_flag"]], "Feature table (original units)", 2)
    return table


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""

HASTS206 Assignment 2, University of Zimbabwe

PART 10 - k-means clustering, diagnostics, stability and dashboard exports (Q4b, Q4c).

  * k = 1..6, n_init = 50 random starts per fit (brief asks for at least 20).
  * WCSS (inertia) and % reduction between successive k.
  * Mean silhouette for k = 2..6 and silhouette plots for two candidates.
  * Stability: (i) a different seed, (ii) overall-median imputation instead of
    KNN, (iii) dropping piped water. Compared with the adjusted Rand index (ARI),
    which ignores how cluster labels are numbered.
  * Profiles: sizes and centroids in original units.
  * Final step: write the tidy CSVs that the Power BI dashboard reads.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score, silhouette_samples, adjusted_rand_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from common import (load_raw, load_settings, show_table, save_table, save_fig, plt, TABLES,
                    DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE, GREY, PALETTE, HYPO, SEED_PRIMARY, SEED_CHECK, N_INIT)
from part09_clustering_features_Shaun_Kanojerera import FEATURES, build_features, knn_impute

CHOSEN_K = 3


def fit(X, k, seed):
    return KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=N_INIT, random_state=seed).fit(X)


def name_clusters(centroids: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Give each cluster a demographic name from its centroid (original units)."""
    names = {}
    old = centroids.share_65plus_pct.idxmax()
    names[old] = "Ageing, natural decrease"
    rest = centroids.drop(index=old)
    hub = rest.nmr_per_1000.idxmax()
    names[hub] = "Working-age in-migration hubs"
    for c in rest.index.drop(hub):
        names[c] = "Young, high fertility, out-migration"
    return names


def silhouette_panel(ax, X, labels, k, colours):
    sil = silhouette_samples(X, labels)
    y = 0
    for c in range(k):
        v = np.sort(sil[labels == c])
        ax.barh(np.arange(y, y + len(v)), v, height=1.0, color=colours[c % len(colours)], edgecolor="white")
        ax.text(-0.08, y + len(v) / 2, f"C{c}", va="center", fontsize=8)
        y += len(v) + 2
    avg = silhouette_score(X, labels)
    ax.axvline(avg, color="red", ls="--", lw=1)
    ax.set_title(f"k = {k}: mean silhouette {avg:.3f}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Silhouette value s(i)")
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_xlim(-0.15, 1)


def main():
    print("Author: Trish Tembo (Clustering Analyst and Dashboard Integrator)")
    print("PART 10: k-means clustering, diagnostics, stability and exports (Q4b-c)")
    s = load_settings()
    feats = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "p09_cluster_features.csv", index_col="district_id")
    X = feats[[f"z_{c}" for c in FEATURES]].to_numpy()

    # ---- 4b diagnostics ------------------------------------------------------
    rows, models = [], {}
    for k in range(1, 7):
        km = fit(X, k, SEED_PRIMARY)
        models[k] = km
        rows.append({"k": k, "WCSS": km.inertia_,
                     "mean_silhouette": silhouette_score(X, km.labels_) if k > 1 else np.nan})
    diag = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    diag["pct_reduction_from_previous_k"] = 100 * (1 - diag.WCSS / diag.WCSS.shift(1))
    show_table(diag, f"k-means diagnostics (n_init = {N_INIT}, seed = {SEED_PRIMARY})", 4)
    save_table(diag, "p10_kmeans_diagnostics.csv")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.5, 3.3))
    axes[0].plot(diag.k, diag.WCSS, marker="o", color=DARK)
    for r in diag.itertuples():
        if r.k > 1:
            axes[0].annotate(f"-{r.pct_reduction_from_previous_k:.0f}%", (r.k, r.WCSS), textcoords="offset points",
                             xytext=(4, 6), fontsize=7.5, color=BLUE)
    axes[0].set_xlabel("Number of clusters k")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Within-cluster sum of squares (standardised units)")
    axes[0].set_title("Elbow plot: WCSS against k")
    d2 = diag.dropna()
    axes[1].bar(d2.k, d2.mean_silhouette, color=[DARK if k == CHOSEN_K else SKY for k in d2.k])
    for r in d2.itertuples():
        axes[1].text(r.k, r.mean_silhouette + 0.01, f"{r.mean_silhouette:.3f}", ha="center", fontsize=8)
    axes[1].set_xlabel("Number of clusters k")
    axes[1].set_ylabel("Mean silhouette")
    axes[1].set_title("Mean silhouette, k = 2 to 6")
    fig.text(0.01, -0.03, HYPO, fontsize=7, color="grey")
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, "fig09_wcss_silhouette.png")

    # Silhouette plots for two plausible candidates
    cand = [2, 3]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.5, 3.8))
    for ax, k in zip(axes, cand):
        silhouette_panel(ax, X, models[k].labels_, k, [DARK, BLUE, SKY, ORANGE])
    fig.suptitle("Individual silhouette values by cluster for the two candidate solutions", fontsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, "fig10_silhouette_candidates.png")
    for k in cand:
        sv = silhouette_samples(X, models[k].labels_)
        print(f"k={k}: min silhouette {sv.min():.3f}, districts with s(i) < 0.1: {int((sv < 0.1).sum())}")

    # ---- 4c chosen k, stability -------------------------------------------------
    km = models[CHOSEN_K]
    labels = km.labels_
    km_seed = fit(X, CHOSEN_K, SEED_CHECK)
    ari_seed = adjusted_rand_score(labels, km_seed.labels_)

    raw = load_raw()
    f2 = build_features(raw["districts"], raw["age_sex"])
    f2["piped_water_pct"] = f2.piped_water_pct.fillna(f2.piped_water_pct.median())   # overall median rule
    X_med = StandardScaler().fit_transform(f2[FEATURES])
    km_med = fit(X_med, CHOSEN_K, SEED_PRIMARY)
    ari_med = adjusted_rand_score(labels, km_med.labels_)

    X_nowater = StandardScaler().fit_transform(feats[FEATURES[:3]])
    km_nw = fit(X_nowater, CHOSEN_K, SEED_PRIMARY)
    ari_nw = adjusted_rand_score(labels, km_nw.labels_)

    def moved(a, b):
        """Districts not in the best-matching renamed cluster (labels can be permuted)."""
        return int(len(a) - pd.crosstab(a, b).max(axis=1).sum())

    stab = pd.DataFrame([
        {"check": f"Different seed ({SEED_CHECK} instead of {SEED_PRIMARY})", "ARI_vs_primary": ari_seed,
         "districts_changing_cluster": moved(labels, km_seed.labels_)},
        {"check": "Overall-median imputation of water (instead of KNN)", "ARI_vs_primary": ari_med,
         "districts_changing_cluster": moved(labels, km_med.labels_)},
        {"check": "Drop piped water (3 demographic features only)", "ARI_vs_primary": ari_nw,
         "districts_changing_cluster": moved(labels, km_nw.labels_)},
    ])
    show_table(stab, f"Stability of the k = {CHOSEN_K} solution (adjusted Rand index)", 3)
    save_table(stab, "p10_stability_checks.csv")
    show_table(pd.crosstab(pd.Series(labels, name="primary"), pd.Series(km_med.labels_, name="median_imputation")),
               "Membership cross-tab: primary vs median imputation (labels may be renamed)")

    # ---- Profiles in original units ----------------------------------------------
    feats["cluster"] = labels
    cent = feats.groupby("cluster")[FEATURES].mean()
    names = name_clusters(cent)
    feats["cluster_name"] = feats.cluster.map(names)
    prof = cent.copy()
    prof["n_districts"] = feats.groupby("cluster").size()
    prof["cluster_name"] = prof.index.map(names)
    prof["districts"] = feats.groupby("cluster").apply(lambda g: ", ".join(g.index), include_groups=False)
    # centroids from the scaler back-transform agree with the plain means (check)
    sc = StandardScaler().fit(feats[FEATURES])
    back = pd.DataFrame(sc.inverse_transform(km.cluster_centers_), columns=FEATURES)
    print(f"Centroid back-transform equals cluster means: {np.allclose(back.to_numpy(), cent.to_numpy())}")
    show_table(prof[["cluster_name", "n_districts"] + FEATURES + ["districts"]], "Cluster sizes and centroids (original units)", 2)
    save_table(prof.reset_index(), "pbi_cluster_centroids.csv")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.9))
    pairs = [("share_u15_pct", "share_65plus_pct", "Share under 15 (%)", "Share aged 65+ (%)"),
             ("nmr_per_1000", "piped_water_pct", "Net migration rate per 1,000 (2025)", "Piped-water access (%)")]
    for ax, (xc, yc, xl, yl) in zip(axes, pairs):
        for c, col in zip(sorted(feats.cluster.unique()), [DARK, ORANGE, SKY]):
            g = feats[feats.cluster == c]
            ax.scatter(g[xc], g[yc], s=45, color=col, alpha=0.9, edgecolor="white",
                       label=f"C{c}: {names[c]} (n={len(g)})")
            cx, cy = g[xc].mean(), g[yc].mean()
            ax.scatter(cx, cy, marker="X", s=110, color="black", zorder=4)
        imp = feats[feats.piped_water_imputed_flag == 1]
        ax.scatter(imp[xc], imp[yc], s=110, facecolor="none", edgecolor="red", lw=1.2,
                   label="Imputed water (D04, D17)")
        ax.set_xlabel(xl)
        ax.set_ylabel(yl)
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=7, loc="upper right")
    fig.suptitle(f"District clusters (k = {CHOSEN_K}); X marks each centroid - {HYPO}", fontsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_fig(fig, "fig11_cluster_map.png")

    # ---- Dashboard exports ---------------------------------------------------------
    bal = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "p04_balance_and_rates_all_districts.csv").set_index("district_id")
    prof_d = bal[["district_name", "region", "population_2020", "population_2025", "population_2026",
                  "births_2025", "deaths_2025", "arrivals_2025", "departures_2025",
                  "reconstructed_2026", "CBR_per_1000", "CDR_per_1000", "RNI_per_1000", "NMR_per_1000",
                  "growth_rate_per_1000"]].join(
        feats[["share_u15_pct", "share_65plus_pct", "piped_water_raw", "piped_water_pct",
               "piped_water_imputed_flag", "cluster", "cluster_name"]])
    prof_d = prof_d.rename(columns={"piped_water_pct": "piped_water_used_pct"})
    prof_d["selected_for_comparison"] = prof_d.index.isin([s["district_a"], s["district_b"]]).astype(int)
    prof_d["projection_district"] = (prof_d.index == s["projection_district"]).astype(int)
    save_table(prof_d.reset_index(), "pbi_district_profiles.csv")

    ags = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "clean_age_sex.csv")
    save_table(ags[["district_id", "age_start", "age_group", "sex", "population_2025"]], "pbi_age_sex_2025.csv")
    save_table(diag, "pbi_kmeans_diagnostics.csv")

    # Figures we reconcile between Python and Power BI
    comp = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "p07_projection_comparison.csv").set_index("method")
    claims = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "p08_expected_claims.csv")
    recon = pd.DataFrame([
        {"figure": "Total population 1 Jan 2025 (24 districts)", "python_value": prof_d.population_2025.sum()},
        {"figure": f"{s['projection_district']} cohort-component Base total 2030",
         "python_value": comp.loc["Cohort-component Base", "P2030"]},
        {"figure": "Expected benefits year 1 (USD)", "python_value": claims.expected_benefits_usd.iloc[0]},
        {"figure": "Expected benefits year 2 (USD)", "python_value": claims.expected_benefits_usd.iloc[1]},
        {"figure": f"Districts in '{names[feats.loc[s['district_b'], 'cluster']]}' cluster",
         "python_value": int((feats.cluster == feats.loc[s['district_b'], 'cluster']).sum())},
    ])
    show_table(recon, "Python figures to reconcile with the Power BI dashboard", 2)
    save_table(recon, "pbi_reconciliation_targets.csv")
    print("\nAll Power BI tables written to outputs/tables/pbi_*.csv")
    return diag, stab, prof


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Choice of k = 3. WCSS falls by 94% from k = 2 to k = 3 and by much less afterwards, and the mean silhouette peaks at k = 3 (0.864) with every district above 0.79, so no district is poorly placed. The three groups also have clear demographic meaning: ageing natural-decrease districts, working-age in-migration hubs with high water access, and young high-fertility districts losing people through migration. Memberships are identical (ARI = 1) under a different seed, under median imputation and without the water feature.

Use: the profiles let planners roll out programmes by district type (for example water investment in the young, low-access group). Limitation: they rest on four 2025 indicators of synthetic data, and the clusters say nothing about change within a district over time.
